clue.text: Be that as it may, everybody is in good health

parts.note: everybody means all
someone in good health is very well

explanation.surface: A grudging concession followed by a cheerful report that the whole family is fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are concessive idioms granting a point before a 'but' follows.

clue.text: Appear dimly in the gloominess

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, the gloominess

explanation.surface: Something faintly visible through the murk.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to come into view as a vague, shadowy shape.

clue.text: We come up after six to watch television?

indicators.note: after places the turned pronoun behind the six in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word we is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group settling in after six o'clock for an evening in front of the box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' turns WE into EW, which follows VI. The question mark marks the definition as a loose example.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to watch, and television audiences are called viewers.

clue.text: Go back to the asylum

definitions.meaning: to withdraw or move backwards, as an army does
a place of refuge or seclusion

explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal from danger and a sanctuary sought for safety share one word.

clue.text: It is just a question of time

definitions.text: It is just a question of time

parts.words: It is just a question of time
parts.note: read literally, this describes the interrogative word you use to ask about time

explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative asking at what time something happens is the simplest question about time.

clue.text: One heard to be without varnish

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken, so we take its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: one to be without something is a lacker, one who lacks it

explanation.surface: Someone who has decided to go without a coat of varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ... to be without' describes a LACKER, one who lacks; 'heard' says that word sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard glossy coating, a kind of varnish.

clue.text: Bury loose cash at the motorway junction

parts.note: to inter is to bury
loose coins in a pocket are change

explanation.surface: Someone burying stolen coins beside a big road intersection.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-level road junction where traffic switches between routes.

clue.text: Idiot's to make a mistake and it's a fruitless journey

parts.note: an idiot is a fool; the possessive gives the s
to err is to make a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a blundering idiot's trip is going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointless mission with no hope of success is an idiom for a wasted trip.

clue.text: Ruin a foreign party

parts.note: un is French for a, a foreign word for it
do is informal for a party

explanation.surface: An overseas celebration spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their downfall.

clue.text: Final stage of house extension!

parts.note: a house is a home
a stretch is an extension

explanation.surface: Builders nearing the end of work on a house extension.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straight of a racecourse, figuratively the closing phase of anything.

clue.text: Prevent the escape of an animal

definitions.meaning: to close something tightly so nothing gets out

explanation.definitionFit: Shutting something tight and the flippered marine mammal share one word.

clue.text: Angry archer?

parts.note: an archer could be called a bowman, and an angry one is cross

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier armed with a mechanical bow, punningly a bowman who is cross.

clue.text: Digger one spotted in the pack?

definitions.text: Digger one spotted in the pack?

parts.words: Digger one spotted in the pack?
parts.note: a spade is a digger, and a card marked with a single pip sits in a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: The single-pip card of the suit named after a digging tool.

clue.text: Claret I distributed during the performance

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of claret I are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wine being handed round during a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetic performance given by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Students decline to learn it

parts.note: decline seems to mean refuse, but students of this classical tongue decline nouns as part of learning it

explanation.definitionFit: Learners of the ancient Roman tongue chant noun declensions.

clue.text: Bill to bleed badly outside and collapse

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters go round the bill
badly says the letters of bleed are scrambled

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bill that leaves one bleeding money, and a financial collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns BLEED into DEBLE; 'outside' wraps it round AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden ignominious failure or collapse.

clue.text: Long narrow trench said in France to be next to the church

parts.note: dit is French for said

explanation.surface: A trench dug alongside a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch is a long narrow channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: Animal trap I replaced

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of trap I are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter resetting a trap for some creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk.

clue.text: Lost new penny in it perhaps

indicators.note: new says the letters of lost are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lost coin, perhaps rolled into a slot machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin slot is the opening a penny is pushed into.

clue.text: 1960s musical that grows on one

definitions.meaning: the 1968 rock musical of the hippie era
what grows on a person's head

explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s rock musical shares its title with what sprouts on one's scalp.

clue.text: A growing form of punishment

parts.note: growing hints at a tree, whose rods were once used to flog offenders

explanation.definitionFit: A tree whose bundled twigs were once used for flogging gave its name to the penalty.

clue.text: Chucker-out employed by Botham perhaps

definitions.meaning: a doorman who throws out unruly customers
a short-pitched ball a fast bowler such as Ian Botham might use

explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham was an English cricket all-rounder; a fast bowler's short delivery that rears up at the batsman has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub doorman and a short, rearing cricket delivery share one name.

clue.text: Diabolical hill he's stumbled upon

indicators.note: stumbled suggests the letters of hill he's tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker tripping on a fiendishly steep hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellish means fiendish, fit for the infernal regions.

clue.text: Musical instrument for singer with nothing on

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
O is the figure nought, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical instrument swapped for a naked singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a deep-toned woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Put a jinx on silver in a six-sided figure

indicators.note: in places the silver inside the other pieces

parts.note: to hex is to put a jinx on
taken as written
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Casting a spell on silver inside a geometric shape, like a witch's charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane figure with six straight sides and six angles.

clue.text: We hear he left show

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: left says he has departed from the word hear

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip that a man has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear a look or expression is to show or display it.

clue.text: Endlessly regretting bankruptcy

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the regretting word is cut off

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so regretting is ruing

explanation.surface: Someone forever lamenting going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial ruin is the state of having lost everything.

clue.text: I entered by the jetty

indicators.note: entered says the I goes into the other word

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone stepping onto a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a structure projecting into the sea, like a jetty.

clue.text: Girl upsetting a clergyman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the pieces upside down so they read bottom to top

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A girl annoying a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns A REV over to make VERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Insisted cur could be examined closely

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of insisted cur could be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog's owner insisting the mongrel be checked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise is to inspect carefully and in detail.

clue.text: Top monkey gets a kiss

parts.note: an ape is a monkey, loosely
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: The leading monkey being given a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip.

clue.text: Pain we get at the baker's shop

definitions.text: Pain we get at the baker's shop

parts.words: Pain we get at the baker's shop
parts.note: pain is the French word for bread, so the pain in a bakery is a Gallic loaf

explanation.definitionFit: The French call bread pain, and the long Gallic loaf is sold in bakeries.
